answer: Jade Trace Fingerprinting. Each identity must publish a continuous stream of signed micro-work whose timing and content are seeded from its own prior outputs; a knob at the knoll of each epoch requires the next seed to derive from the last verified artifact. Duplicates cannot share history, so a clone either diverges (detectable fork) or must replay the original's whole verified lineage. The willow of cost: an attacker pays full compute and storage to reproduce every prior artifact per Sybil, making N copies cost N times one honest identity's lifetime work.
